statement: A bakery has $60$ cups of flour. Each loaf of bread uses $3$ cups of flour and each tray of muffins uses $2$ cups. The equation $3b + 2m = 60$ describes the numbers of loaves $b$ and trays $m$ that use all of the flour. If the bakery makes $14$ loaves of bread, how many trays of muffins can it make with the flour that is left?

choices.misconception: I found the 18 cups of flour left over and gave that as the answer without dividing by the 2 cups each tray needs.
I subtracted the 14 loaves straight from the 60 cups, so I got $(60 - 14) \div 2 = 23$, but the loaves use 3 cups each.
I used all 60 cups for muffins, $60 \div 2 = 30$, and forgot that the bread had already used some flour.

hints: Find how much flour the bread uses, then see how many trays the rest makes.
$3(14) = 42$ cups go to bread, leaving $60 - 42 = 18$ cups. Each tray uses $2$ cups.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
